subject: Post-demo: Differentiator matrix + proposed smoke validation plan
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@optihealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@optihealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Differentiator matrix + proposed smoke validation plan

Hi Daniel / Priya —

Great to connect earlier — thanks for the candid discussion and for walking us through OptiHealth's top priorities. Per our call I wanted to capture the key pain points, how Redwood maps to your decision criteria, and propose concrete next steps so we all have the same checklist for the bake-off.

Quick summary of what we heard (you can correct me if I missed anything):
- Core pain: inconsistent latency at peak times causing timeouts for patient-facing summaries; current infra is costly at scale and lacks predictable SLAs.
- Decision priorities: 1) P99 latency under 600ms for 512-token prompts, 2) per-token cost under $0.0009 (target), 3) model quality parity with current vendor on clinical extraction tasks, 4) SOC2 + audit logs, 5) private deployment option for PHI workflows.
- Open questions we captured: what fraction of requests are bursty vs steady? (you said ~30% bursts off-hours), and whether you can share one redacted prompt set for QA.

What we delivered on the call:
- Live demo of the hosting runtime showing steady-state latency and fallback behavior.
- A quick differentiator matrix comparing Redwood vs Vendor A and Vendor B on your top five dimensions (attached).

Proposed next steps (short timeline):
1) OptiHealth to share a representative prompt set (redacted) and sample traffic profile — due Fri 5/21.
2) Redwood to run a two-day smoke-validation against a 3-candidate matrix: Redwood hosted, Redwood private (single-node), and your incumbent Vendor A. Tests: latency distribution, end-to-end P99, and cost-per-token estimate. Deliverable: short report + recordings — ETA Wed 5/26.
3) Camila (SE) to define the smoke-test recipe and list any infra access or artifacts needed.
4) Quick calibration call after we have test results — propose Mon 5/31 10am PT.

Attachments: differentiator_matrix_v1.xlsx (high-level comparison), smoke_test_recipe.md (draft checklist).

Questions for you now:
- Can you confirm you’re comfortable with the candidate matrix above (hosted, private single-node, Vendor A)?
- Will you be able to provide the redacted prompts and a brief traffic histogram by Friday?

Thanks again — excited to run these tests and show measurable differences.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

--

From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@optihealth.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Differentiator matrix + proposed smoke validation plan

Thanks Rafael — good write-up and the matrix helps a lot. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Prompt set: we can share a redacted set of ~120 prompts (mix of extraction, summarization, and triage classification). We'll strip PHI and send a link to a Drive folder by EOD Friday (5/21).
2) Traffic profile: the 30% burst estimate was accurate — bursts are typically 200–400 RPS sustained for 3–8 minutes during certain campaign windows. Baseline steady is ~40 RPS.
3) Regarding the candidate matrix: Vendor B is less important for us — we mainly want a tight comparison vs Vendor A + Redwood options. Fine to proceed with the 3 candidates you proposed.

One ask: could you add a test that measures tokenization differences and any cost delta that comes from different tokenizers? We've seen surprise costs there.

We'll confirm the Drive link Friday and aim to join the post-test calibration call on 5/31.

—Daniel
Director of Platform Engineering | OptiHealth
daniel.cho@optihealth.com

Thanks Rafael — I updated the recipe and attached a short checklist. Summary of changes and plan: 

Planned smoke-validation scope (2 days):
- Candidate environments: Redwood hosted (prod-like cluster), Redwood private (single-node, quantized), Vendor A (incumbent, equivalent instance).
- Tests:
  - Latency sweep: 64 / 128 / 256 / 512 tokens (measure p50/p95/p99).
  - Burst behavior: simulate 40 RPS baseline with 200/300/400 RPS bursts (3–8 minute holds) to capture queueing and degradation patterns.
  - Tokenization delta: run tokenizer on prompt set across models, compare token counts and downstream cost projection.
  - Quality sanity checks: run 20 representative extraction prompts and compare labeled fields (precision/recall) to Vendor A.
  - Audit trail: collect request tracing and audit logs (where available) for SOC2 evidence.

Infrastructure & artifacts needed from OptiHealth:
- Redacted prompt set (S3 or Drive link) — we will process in a temporary, encrypted test bucket and delete after the run.
- An admin contact for Vendor A access if they want us to coordinate the vendor-run tests (opt-in).

Deliverables:
- Short report (PDF) with latency and cost graphs, tokenization delta table, and quality sanity check results.
- Replayable test recipe + scripts + raw logs (archived).

Attachments: smoke_test_recipe.md (updated), quick-ops-checklist.txt (ops runbook).

I will kick off infra for the hosted and private runs on Monday morning (5/24) so we have warm nodes for Wed's runs. Rafael / Marissa — I will drop links to the Drive folder and HubSpot tasks when I post the final recipe.

Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
